matches.rationale: No finding captures the issue of unrealistically large SR improvements and lack of variability/ablation in Section 4.1. Findings 1 and 2 report opposite text–table inconsistencies (claiming modest gains vs. table showing large gains) rather than the inflated gains in the ground truth.

Finding 7 identifies that Eq. (1) omits the Frustum Culling removal while the method states outdated points are removed, exposing the same logical inconsistency in the 3D representation update logic described in the ground truth.
No finding addresses the exaggerated claim that prior 3D segmentation methods focus only on mask accuracy, nor the overstatement of Dynam3D's semantic alignment novelty in the Introduction.

Finding 8 notes that without stricter evaluation protocols the reported pre-exploration and lifelong memory gains may be inflated by environment memorization or data leakage, exactly matching the ground truth concern about omitted controls in Section 4.2.
None of the findings mention missing ethical approvals, consent, or safety protocols in the real-world robot experiments, so the ethical integrity omission is undetected.

Finding 8 shows the abstract's claim that pre-exploration and lifelong memory experiments validate practical deployment is stronger than the caveats in Section 4.2, mirroring the ground truth's identification of rhetorical overstatement in the abstract about practical significance.

No finding captures the subtle reference misuse in Related Work where concurrent works addressing similar spatial comprehension limitations are ignored; finding 6 addresses a duplicate citation issue, which is unrelated.
No finding discusses the Conclusion's overreaching claim of strong generalization given only preliminary real-world tests, so the context misalignment in Section 5 is not matched.

Finding 5 reveals that the text claims an ablation on 3D instance/zone embedding degradation but Table 7 lacks those results, directly corresponding to the ground truth's criticism that noise robustness experiments do not explore degradation of the 3D representation itself.
No finding reports the absence of ethical use, consent, or data privacy statements in the appendix's dataset collection details, leaving this ethical omission undetected.

None of the findings point out the lack of quantitative metrics for memory saturation, update latency, or forgetting in the claim about balancing real-time adaptability and long-term memory; the issue is not captured.

No finding addresses the absolutist language in the Introduction's contribution bullet (e.g., 'achieves state-of-the-art performance' without caveats), so this rhetorical overstatement remains unmatched.
